subject: Estimate the overall population of passerines using pcount - unmarked

messages.author: c9a0bb51cea1df8f
messages.subject: Estimate the overall population of passerines using pcount - unmarked
parts:
Hello,

First of all, I apologize if someone already answered the question I'm about to ask, but I couldn't find it. This is the first time I use unmarked.

A quick explanation of my study. I'm studying the abundance of four passerine species using point counts survey in a defined area (27 000 hectares). 178 points (100 meters radius) have been visited two times in the past few weeks. Note that same points has already been visited in 2014.
We recorded the proportion of different habitats on each site to study its influence on bird's abundance. We also recorded various covariates as time, date, weather, or observer to take the effect of these covariates on the detection probability into consideration.

Our objective is to determine whether the overall population of each specie has changed between 2014 or not, and whether abundance changes between habitats or not.

After processing various N-mixture models using pcount, I selected a top model based on AIC (here is my best model) :

>summary(bestmod)

I cut the study area with a grid of the exact same size as points count area (177 x177 m approximately). In each square of the grid, I have the information for the proportion of each habitat I tested in different models.

Then, I used the best model to predict abundance of the specie in all grid squares using predict ("habitat_square" is a dataframe containing the proportion of habitats in each square)  :

>square.abundance<-predict(bestmod,newdata=habitat_square[,-1],type="state",backTransform = TRUE)
>head(square.abundance)
   Predicted         SE     lower     upper
1 0.04569522 0.02136447 0.0182767 0.1142467

5 0.04569522 0.02136447 0.0182767 0.1142467
6 0.04569522 0.02136447 0.0182767 0.1142467

My question are : is it correct to say that the overall population estimate is the sum of the abundance estimate in each square ? Is it correct, then, to say that the overall population SE is the sum of SEs for each square ? Actually, I don't really understand how predict is able to give a standard error for each prediction. 
Finally, may I conclude, if estimates and SEs for the overall population in 2014 and 2018 are really different, that the population changed (increased or decreased) ? Should I use confidence intervall instead of SE ?

I hope I have been clear enough,
Thanks in advance for your help, all best,

Aurel
